title: What If You Never Looked Up From Your Phone?

scenes.text: What if you never looked up from your phone? Your neck would carry a second head.
Your head weighs about ten to twelve pounds when it sits straight over your shoulders.
Tilt it forward fifteen degrees, and the load on your neck jumps to about twenty-seven pounds.
At forty-five degrees it's about forty-nine pounds. At sixty, the usual phone angle, about sixty pounds.
A spine surgeon calculated this in 2014. Hours a day, that adds up to hundreds of hours a year.
Sixty pounds is roughly an eight-year-old child. Now lift your phone to eye level.

description:
What if you never looked up from your phone? A 2014 model by spine surgeon Kenneth Hansraj estimated the load on the neck: about 10 to 12 pounds upright, 27 at 15 degrees, 40 at 30, 49 at 45 and 60 pounds at 60 degrees of forward tilt.
People spend hours a day in this posture, which adds up to hundreds of hours a year.
